overall_summary: Space and planetary mysteries showcasing extreme cosmic environments are the channel's clear primary growth driver, consistently generating the highest view counts and engagement. Conversely, cognitive psychology and brain-related facts underperform significantly, with repetitive uploads of the same concepts leading to severe audience fatigue and near-zero reach.

winning_patterns.evidence: The Planet Darker Than Coal (TrES-2b) achieved 1,018 views and 36 likes, This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies reached 721 views and 25 likes, and The Planet of Burning Ice generated 1,055 views.
winning_patterns.action: Focus content production heavily on extreme exoplanets, bizarre space physics, and cosmic anomalies. Standardize the duration to 19-21 seconds to allow for deeper visual storytelling and build-up.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' was uploaded three times across different dates, yielding only 53, 5, and 11 views respectively. 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' stagnated at 38 views.
weak_patterns.action: De-prioritize basic human psychology topics and strictly enforce a rule against re-uploading identical concepts or titles within a 30-day window.

next_video.concept: The Planet Orbiting a Black Hole Where One Hour is 7 Years
next_video.opening_direction: Imagine landing on a planet where taking a quick 10-minute walk means everyone you love back on Earth has been dead for decades.
next_video.twist_direction: But the terrifying part isn't the lost time—it's that the black hole's gravity pulls the ocean into skyscraper-sized vertical walls of water.
next_video.reason: Leverages the highly successful extreme space category using a proven 21-second format. It introduces a high-stakes 'what-if' survival element to maximize viewer retention from the very first second.

experiment: Test a cinematic space survival concept ('What If You Fell Into Jupiter's Liquid Metal Ocean?') to see if combining the high-performing space niche with cinematic survival storytelling yields higher average retention than standard exoplanet profiles.
